quick.description: Server exposes tools with no authentication declared. Any caller — including unrelated agents — can invoke every tool.
quick.remediation: Declare an auth block (api_key, oauth2, or mtls) and refuse unauthenticated requests at the transport layer.

quick.description: Server transport is plain HTTP. Bearer tokens and tool payloads are exposed on the wire to any party between caller and server.
quick.remediation: Move the listener behind TLS (HTTPS or HTTPS-fronted reverse proxy). Reject plaintext upgrades.

quick.description: A destructive tool (delete / drop / purge / wipe) is invokable without an explicit confirmation flag.
quick.remediation: Require a typed confirmation parameter (e.g. confirm_token: 'DELETE') and validate server-side before executing.

quick.description: An export-style tool returns an unbounded set of records (no row cap, no time window).
quick.remediation: Cap export tools to a maximum row count and require a time window. Prefer paginated retrieval for large data sets.

quick.description: No rate limiting is declared. A misbehaving or rogue caller can saturate the server, exhausting upstream provider quotas.
quick.remediation: Declare per-principal request budgets at the manifest layer and enforce them at the transport.

deep.description: Manifest version is pre-1.0 (`0.x`). The tool surface is not contractually stable and callers cannot pin confidently.
deep.remediation: Cut a 1.0 release once the tool surface stabilises. Use semver to signal breaking changes.

deep.description: The manifest name has no publisher/vendor namespace. Authorship and trust attribution are ambiguous.
deep.remediation: Namespace the server name (e.g. `helixar/inspector`). Publish under a verified vendor identity.

deep.description: OAuth scopes are coarse-grained — the declared scopes do not separate read from write. One scope grants every capability.
deep.remediation: Split scopes by verb and object (e.g. `read:messages`, `write:messages`). Assign the narrowest verb a tool can tolerate.

quick.description: A tool surfaces personally-identifiable information by name (SSN, DOB, full address, card numbers).
quick.remediation: Filter PII at the tool boundary. Return tokenised or redacted views; serve raw PII only behind a stricter scope.
quick.evidence: PII keywords surfaced: ssn, date_of_birth, credit_card, address

quick.description: A tool description contains prompt-injection phrasing aimed at the calling model (e.g. 'ignore previous instructions').
quick.remediation: Strip or sanitise tool descriptions before they reach the model. Reject manifests whose descriptions look like instructions.
quick.evidence: injection-shaped phrase(s): ignore previous instructions | unconditionally

deep.description: A tool fetches arbitrary external URLs supplied by the caller. The server becomes a confused-deputy proxy to anywhere on the internet (SSRF).
deep.remediation: Constrain outbound URLs to a documented allowlist. Reject private ranges and metadata endpoints at the server.
